table.name: Friend
table.purpose: Friendship pairs between high schoolers: each row links one student (col_001) to another student (col_002) they are friends with, referencing the Highschooler table. Likely the classic social-network schema (Highschooler, Friend, Likes).

col_001.name: student_id
col_001.description: ID of one high schooler in the friendship pair; references Highschooler.col_001 (student ID).

col_002.name: friend_id
col_002.description: ID of the other high schooler in the friendship pair; references Highschooler.col_001 (student ID). Which of the two columns is 'student' vs 'friend' is arbitrary since friendship is symmetric.

table.name: Highschooler
table.purpose: A lookup/entity table of high school students, one row per student, referenced by the Friend and Likes tables (which record friendships and likes between students).

col_001.name: student_id
col_001.description: Primary key: unique numeric identifier for each high school student. Referenced by Friend and Likes tables to identify the student in a friendship or like relationship.

col_002.name: name
col_002.description: The student's first name. Not unique (e.g., Gabriel and Jordan appear twice).

col_003.name: grade
col_003.description: The student's grade level (year in school), values 9-12 (freshman through senior), evenly distributed with 4 students per grade.

table.name: Likes
table.purpose: Edge table recording which high schooler likes which high schooler (a social-network 'likes' relation). Each row is a directed like from one student to another; col_001 is the liker and col_002 the liked student. The primary key on col_001 suggests each student appears as a liker at most once in this sample, though the table likely allows multiple likes in general.

col_001.name: liker_id
col_001.description: ID of the high schooler who likes someone (the source of the like). References Highschooler.col_001 (student ID). Declared primary key here, so each student appears as a liker at most once.

col_002.name: liked_id
col_002.description: ID of the high schooler who is liked (the target of the like). References Highschooler.col_001. Many-to-one: several students can like the same person (e.g. 1468 and 1709 are each liked twice).
